title: Linear Inequalities: Solving and Showing Solutions on the Number Line
seo_title: Linear Inequalities Class 11 Worksheet with Answers (NCERT Chapter 5)
standard_text: Linear inequalities; algebraic solutions of linear inequalities in one variable and their representation on the number line (summary of the CBSE syllabus)
meta_desc: Class 11 Linear Inequalities worksheet (NCERT Chapter 5): solving in one variable, interval answers, solutions in N and Z, the number line, double inequalities and word problems. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Multiplying or dividing by a negative number reverses the sign.
key_sub: Strict signs (<, >) leave the end point out.
body_html:
How it works

  • You may add or subtract the same number on both sides.
  • You may multiply or divide both sides by a positive number; for a negative number, reverse the sign.
  • On the number line, < and > use an open circle; ≤ and ≥ use a filled circle.
  • Interval form: x < 3 is (−∞, 3); x ≥ 3 is [3, ∞).
Example

Solve 3 − 2x ≤ 9.

−2x ≤ 6

Divide by −2 and reverse: x ≥ −3

Answer: [−3, ∞)

Common mistakes

  • Not reversing the sign when dividing by a negative number.
  • Using [ ] for a strict inequality.
  • Including 0 among the natural numbers.

items.q: A lift can carry at most 600 kg. A worker of mass 60 kg rides with boxes of 24 kg each. What is the greatest number of boxes?
items.e: 60 + 24n ≤ 600, so n ≤ 22.50. The greatest whole number is 22.

items.q: A taxi charges ₹4.30 plus ₹0.50 for every 400 m. Isha has ₹30. What is the greatest number of 400 m stages she can pay for?
items.e: ₹4.30 + ₹0.50n ≤ ₹30 gives n ≤ 51.40. The greatest whole number is 51.
